faq.question: Is a Master’s in Electronics Engineering available in Mauritius?
faq.answer: A dedicated Master’s in Electronics Engineering is not listed in the University of Mauritius’s published 2026–2027 programme list reviewed for this article. Related options include MSc Renewable Energy and Smart Electrical Systems and programmes in Industrial Internet of Things. Students searching for Master’s in Electronics Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students should compare these related courses carefully.

faq.question: Which university should I consider for a related course?
faq.answer: Start by comparing the University of Mauritius and Université des Mascareignes. These are among the Electronics Engineering Universities in Mauritius to explore for related postgraduate options. Review the official course structure, entry criteria, tuition fees and current intake before selecting a programme.

faq.question: What is the cost of living for students in Mauritius?
faq.answer: As a planning estimate, allow around MUR 15,000–25,000 per month, approximately ₹30,000–₹50,000 at the illustrative exchange rate used here. Your actual expenses may be higher or lower depending on housing and lifestyle.

faq.question: Can Indian students apply for postgraduate engineering programmes in Mauritius?
faq.answer: International applicants should check the chosen university’s international admissions requirements, qualification recognition, fees and any applicable study-permit conditions. Eligibility is determined by the institution and the specific programme.

faq.question: What jobs can I pursue after a related master’s degree?
faq.answer: Depending on your specialisation and experience, you may explore roles in electronics design, embedded systems, telecommunications, IoT, automation or research and development. Check that the programme provides the technical subjects and practical experience required for your target role.
